children: Tuas's bull at Citi sees potential for an expedited resolution to the Singapore-focused telecommunications provider's regulatory issues. Analyst Siraj Ahmed says that Tuas-owned Simba has struck a conciliatory tone with regulators over its unauthorized use of mobile spectrum, opting not to dispute the allegations and removing its CEO from its board. Ahmed thinks this response could help speed the process. He reckons the most likely outcome is that Simba will get to keep its mobile license, but warns that this is far from certain. Citi keeps a buy rating on the stock and lowers its target price 22% to 2.30 Australian dollars. Shares are up 1.8% at A$1.40. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
